gen_risks.description: Procurement and installation of modern training equipment and connectivity upgrades may be delayed, limiting institution capacity.
gen_risks.mitigation: Prepare detailed procurement schedule, use fast‑track procedures, and centralize oversight through AFAP with milestone‑based payments.
gen_risks.evidence: The project will finance targeted physical investments... procurement of new modern training equipment and connectivity upgrades.

gen_risks.description: Integrated labour‑market information system and Employability Portal may fail to become operational, reducing job‑matching effectiveness.
gen_risks.mitigation: Hire qualified IT staff early, adopt a phased development and pilot testing approach, and ensure backup power for system resilience.
gen_risks.evidence: The project will help redesign and operationalize an integrated labor market information... new information and data management system... digital Employability Portal.

gen_risks.description: Construction of the new multi‑use training centre on Príncipe may face delays or quality issues, jeopardising EDGE certification.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement a detailed construction schedule with milestone payments, require performance bonds, and conduct regular quality and climate‑resilience inspections.
gen_risks.evidence: Construction of a new multi‑use technical training center... aim to meet EDGE certification and integrate climate‑resilient design.

gen_risks.description: Delays in financial reporting and internal audit could weaken fiduciary controls.
gen_risks.mitigation: Appoint an experienced accountant, customize the accounting system for timely reporting, and schedule regular internal audits.
gen_risks.evidence: Financial management risks identified include delays in recording financial transactions and generating financial reports.

gen_risks.description: Disbursement may be delayed due to Designated Account management or late IFR submissions.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish a clear IFR calendar, train AFAP staff on procedures, and monitor cash‑flow weekly to anticipate shortfalls.
gen_risks.evidence: AFAP will open and manage a designated account... disbursement based on quarterly IFRs.

gen_risks.description: Required specialists (environmental, social, TVET, Data/IT) may not be hired within the 45‑60 day window.
gen_risks.mitigation: Pre‑qualify candidates, use short‑term contracts, and include recruitment penalties for missed deadlines.
gen_risks.evidence: The Recipient shall cause AFAP to hire... an Environmental Specialist... within forty‑five days after Effectiveness.

gen_risks.description: Procurement and rehabilitation works could overrun the planned schedule, affecting overall project timing.
gen_risks.mitigation: Prepare tender documents early, apply accelerated procurement where allowed, and conduct monthly progress reviews.
gen_risks.evidence: The cost estimate for the new center... adjustments will be managed within the project’s procurement plan.

gen_risks.description: Insufficient private‑sector engagement may lead to curricula that do not match labour‑market needs.
gen_risks.mitigation: Formalize Workforce Development Committees, provide employer incentives, and hold quarterly curriculum alignment workshops.
gen_risks.evidence: Workforce Development Committees... bringing together private sector employers, training institutions, relevant ministries, and worker representatives.

gen_risks.description: Gender‑based violence, sexual exploitation or harassment could affect female participants.
gen_risks.mitigation: Hire a qualified GBV/SEA specialist, enforce a strict safeguarding policy, and conduct regular trainings and monitoring.
gen_risks.evidence: The Recipient shall cause AFAP to hire... a Social Specialist with gender‑based violence (GBV) / sexual exploitation and abuse–sexual harassment (SEA/SH) expertise.

gen_risks.description: Grievance Redress Mechanism may not resolve complaints promptly, undermining beneficiary trust.
gen_risks.mitigation: Set clear resolution timelines, publish GRM performance statistics, and train staff on case handling procedures.
gen_risks.evidence: Share of grievances received through the Grievance Redress Mechanism that are resolved on time (Percentage).

gen_risks.description: Activation of the Contingent Emergency Response Component could be delayed by procedural approvals.
gen_risks.mitigation: Draft the CERC Manual before effectiveness, run simulation exercises, and obtain pre‑approval from the World Bank.
gen_risks.evidence: The project will ensure that a manual (“CERC Manual”) is prepared and adopted... activation subject to World Bank agreement.

gen_risks.description: Procurement delays may arise from poor coordination between AFAP and ministries for technical specifications.
gen_risks.mitigation: Hold joint planning workshops, assign a liaison officer, and develop detailed TORs early in the process.
gen_risks.evidence: Procurement will be carried out in accordance with World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers... technical inputs required from ministries.

gen_risks.description: Climate‑related events (floods, storms) could disrupt construction or training activities.
gen_risks.mitigation: Incorporate climate‑resilient design, procure backup generators, and build flexibility into activity schedules.
gen_risks.evidence: STP is vulnerable to coastal floods, severe storms, landslides, and droughts... climate hazards may affect infrastructure and livelihoods.

gen_risks.description: Generation of solid waste and construction debris may cause local environmental impacts.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement a waste‑management plan, require contractors to follow approved disposal procedures, and conduct regular site inspections.
gen_risks.evidence: Project activities may result in the generation of solid waste, obsolete equipment, and minor construction debris.

gen_risks.description: Limited capacity of MLSSS/DTEFP to manage new systems and increased workload could hinder implementation.
gen_risks.mitigation: Deliver targeted capacity‑building, hire a Data/IT assistant, and provide on‑the‑job mentorship for new processes.
gen_risks.evidence: STP’s skills‑building ecosystem suffers from limited capacity, infrastructure constraints, and insufficient alignment with labor demand.

gen_risks.description: PIU restructuring may create coordination gaps between the youth project and the SPRRP.
gen_risks.mitigation: Develop a clear transition plan, define governance roles, and hold weekly coordination meetings during the restructuring period.
gen_risks.evidence: The PIU will be restructured and strengthened to serve as a unified PIU... recruitment of additional senior specialists and assistants.

gen_risks.description: Macro‑economic shocks (fuel/food price volatility, ODA fluctuations) could affect project financing or beneficiary livelihoods.
gen_risks.mitigation: Maintain a contingency buffer in the budget, adopt flexible financing arrangements, and monitor macro‑economic indicators regularly.
gen_risks.evidence: Slow economic growth and covariate shocks... COVID‑19 pandemic, geopolitical turmoil, recurrent flooding, and electricity crisis.

gen_risks.description: Low private‑sector demand in priority value chains may limit job placement for trained youth.
gen_risks.mitigation: Conduct regular labour‑market analyses, adjust training packages to emerging demand, and promote sector reforms and employer incentives.
gen_risks.evidence: Key sectoral challenges relate to infrastructure, sustainable management, destination promotion, and the availability of an adequately prepared workforce.

gt_risks.description: Frequent government changes and the cross-ministerial nature of the jobs agenda can shift policy direction, counterpart arrangements, and implementation momentum; further changes may follow the mid-2026 legislative/parliamentary elections. Success depends on sustained coordination across labor, education, tourism, agriculture, and finance ministries plus private-sector engagement.
gt_risks.mitigation: Anchor the project within MLSSS (core employment-promotion mandate); strengthen technical ownership at directorate level rather than relying on political leadership; establish a formal coordination committee and a unified PIU; continue policy dialogue with Government during implementation.

gt_risks.description: STP's fragile growth outlook, narrow fiscal space, and dependence on external financing leave it highly vulnerable to external shocks (energy/food price swings, donor-disbursement delays, climate events), which may weaken labor demand, reduce firms' absorption capacity, and constrain the Government's ability to sustain recurrent-cost interventions (training, stipends, employment services).
gt_risks.mitigation: Prioritize low-cost, scalable interventions; combine supply-side investments with direct job-creation support; target sectors with growth potential and external demand linkages (incl. labor mobility); coordinate with other World Bank macro-fiscal/energy/private-sector engagements in STP.

gt_risks.description: Limited experience of MLSSS and DTEFP in delivering complex labor-market interventions at scale; fragmented institutional landscape; multiple implementation partners; nascent capacity in labor-market analytics, employment intermediation, and cross-sectoral coordination; sustainability risk if new systems/programs are not institutionalized within government structures and budgets.
gt_risks.mitigation: Leverage existing institutions/mechanisms rather than parallel structures (existing MLSSS PIU, coordination committee, AFAP for fiduciary/safeguards); finance targeted TA and staffing; invest in durable institutional assets (labor-market information system, employability portal, strengthened training institutions, formalized service-provider arrangements); use the learning agenda and impact evaluation to identify cost-effective interventions for scale-up.

gt_risks.description: Complex procurement in a small-island context: residual FM risk is moderate but residual procurement risk is substantial, driven by the complexity of civil works in a remote island context, the large number of technical-assistance contracts, and the multiplicity of projects already handled by AFAP.
gt_risks.mitigation: Agree ToRs and technical specifications between AFAP and the World Bank before initiating any procurement (prior and post-review); reinforce AFAP procurement and contract-management capacity incl. specialized support for civil-works supervision; embed dedicated fiduciary controls for the grants/stipends payment mechanism in the Project Operations Manual; continue and adapt the risk assessment during implementation.
